Hi Evrybody,

I'm forex trader from Poland. I started to learn about trading two
years ago. On the begining it was only my hobby, but few months ago,
after I disvovered RTM I'm treating it much more serious. I want to
change my life by being very succesful trader.

My biggest problem in trading is that I'm impatient and I'm afraid that I
will miss great entry. More screen time and experiance is required I
think. I also will not take TT when there is no engulf or CP on
approach.

My another problem is that I look at the charts all the time and I still
didn't read some grat journals. I think that you can learn many things
directly from the charts, but reading great stuff posted by great trades
can speed up learning process. Another thing is that I'm quite good at
reading charts and recognizing patterns but not always

do I know why something happens. I see that it works on the charts and
repeats all the time but now I want to understand everythig. I want to
know what IT's are doing and why.

So now I'll focus on reading journals and other materials here to
completely understand how market works. Then I'll work on decision
process and train on Forex Tester.

After that I'll trade my first small live account. I want to do this in a
month. So I'll start trading live in end of June or in July if I'll
need some more time.

Hi everyone

I'm happy to be back and thank you IF for putting me on the list.

I decided to start a new journal here, but this time it will be more
results oriented. I'm going to post my statements regularly regardless
of how good/bad it is. The reason for that is that I want to be honest
about my performance in order to not create unrealistic expectations for
new members - that can happen when winning trades are posted (mostly)
and great setups explained. It all looks logical and easy in hindsight
but even though I have a good understanding, in real time I have doubts

Where do I look for trades?

What I aim to do is to take touch trades in the direction of the trend.
But by trend, I mean situation when the price is coming from a valid
zone and didn't reach the target yet. I basically try to find places for
a touch trade after continuation engulfs. I do this when ITs have
positions open and add on retraces by stopping traders out. When I see
that price is reacting to valid target and there is some kind of
reversal I assume ITs are short (for example) and then I look for
opportunities to join the move. So even though most of my trades can be
classified as continuation trades, all of them are reversal trades at
the same time - because if I sell, I sell against strong (usually)
bullish move on smaller scale, and vice versa.

It is important to analyze all scales and to make sure that you are not
trading against direction signaled by engulf on a higher scale.

I have currently one trade open on eurusd, that I didn't explain in my
last post. It is a nice example of continuation trade. I noticed some
time ago that there are a lot of continuation opportunities after
breaking QM levels. And there is a good reason for that so this setup
gives me a nice opportunity to elaborate on that.

I try to look at price more in terms of orders opened by ITs. So at this
point, we can say that there was a quasimodo, and then more shorts were
opened on the way down (see my last post). The idea for continuation or
at least bounce from broken QM lvl seems logical to me. Because I ask
myself this - what needs to happen for QM lvl to be broken? We know that
people get trapped and orders remain at the level - in this case, buy
orders. If ITs want to push the price down they need to sell against buy
orders. So they have shorts orders open at the level. If price goes
above this price level then it means that they will get into drawdown on
these positions. They don't want drawdown, so they will protect this
level by adding shorts and pushing price down.

There are also other things to consider, for example - had ITs have a
chance to reverse positions already? or is there a better place for
retrace? You can see on my chart that there is no obvious better place
for retrace (CP).

This eurusd chart is beautiful, setups are rarely this clean. Its still
possible that I am wrong of course. But thinking about orders in this
way will allow for great trades when your read is correct.

So what I learned is that compression is a great indicator of where you
can expect short retrace. Sometimes price moves from a target area, and
didn't reach the opposite target, and there is "no space" for deep
retraces - so you can get in on the move on short RT.

unintentionally developed a habit of entering many times with small lots

- entering before FL (fear of missing out), and then adding more when the price gets closer to MPL

- being afraid to enter with full risk before price reacts to a level
and. Seeing price bounce gives me a feeling of being correct, so I
enter. But this feeling is not really based on my knowledge. We need to anticipate and not react

of price rising occur, and same goes for shorts. I think that most of
traders experience this - when the price is moving up it feels like it
will countinue, and vice versa. Sometimes even direction of the last M1
candle influences how I feel about my trade. I need to learn to ignore
this feeling.

- not being prepared for entry beforehand. When this happens I see price
reacting to something, then I do analysis, I find out that price is
reacting to a MPL of some important level and then I try to enter

I think that using only pending orders is the way to go. Using
pending orders means that I was prepared for entry and I anticipate what
will happen, and I was completely prepared with my analysis beforehand
instead of reacting to what price is currently doing.

because I try to recover from losses. Of course, it doesn't happen and I
only lose more. This happens when I am strongly convinced that price
didn't hit the TG yet, and I am often right, but the problem with
catching swings is that:

- I ignore good entry points - because I don't want to miss the obvious move

- I don't take partial profits

- I move my stops because there is still valid engulf signal that didn't play out yet or I enter soon after being stopped out

- I don't wait for deepest possible RT

I realized recently that I'm pretty bad at decision making, I'm not
patient enough on live charts, and I tend to make the same mistakes many
times due to loose analysis.

So I set some rules regarding my analysis during practise on FT2:

I test one pair at a time and I have 3 separate charts. One is for
general HTF view and I mark most important lvls and FLs on it.

Second chart is for LTF FL analysis - sometimes it gets messy and that is why I need more than one chart.

On third chart I mark S/R flips, swaps lvls - it is easy to miss them when chart is not neat and clean.

Doing this I'm sure that I used propely my best analysis tools, and I wont do mistakes that could easily been avoided.

And this is how I'm going to improve my decision making:

- I take screenshots with my analysis and mark best places to look for PA

- as price is approaching my lvl, I make decision - do I wait for
confirmation or can I TT? why? I write this on screenshot. Decision is
made.

- let's say that I took TT. At this point I have marked on chart
different sized FL that were formed on approach - I decide where is my
TP1 and where

are potential trouble areas

- I make screen after TP1 , and then after every continuation ENG, or reversal ENG.

- reversal ENG - I close my trade

- continuation ENG - I make decision - where I'll let price retrace to, before closing my trade? where in next FL?

As price is moving away (or towards) my entry I mark new FLs that are
created, I mark CP, and strong SD lvls / ignored SD lvls, using always

the same colors. I don't want to miss/ forget anything. Also I do this to develop habists:

strong SD lvls formed against me ----> look for exit

CP between my entry, and current price ----> I move my SL above last fresh SD lvl

FL not engulfed --> exit

etc.

I know that this is basic stuff, but sometimes I ignored important
information, because I wanted my FL analysis to be correct every single
time.

Its stupid, I know, but I have done this in the past on live account

Every trade is narrated, and I also try to think like IT - what they want to accomplish, where is LQ for them

- what are doing trend followers?

- what are doing BO traders?

- what are doing savy SD traders?

In the next month I will continue practising in this way, and what is
most important - I also want to apply this method to live charts.

In this way I will have everything propely analysed, and decisions will be made only once - I wont stay undecided at any time.

Analysis is made ---> its time to make decisions and write it down.

New piece of PA created --> make analysis marking FLs, SD, CPs ---> make decision, just like on FT2
